title: RampKit Bridge: Codelab Manifest & Sprint Planner (draft)
content:
Purpose and context:
This working doc defines the RampKit Bridge codelab manifest: a small, reproducible curriculum that bridges the SDK quickstart experience to a production-like integration path (local dev -> sandbox -> CI -> observability). Goal is to make the first 60 minutes for an engineer meaningful: ship a tiny app that calls Redwood, collects token/latency telemetry, and exercises fallback/timeout policies.

Audience:
- New SDK adopters (engineers evaluating Redwood for prototyping)
- Internal advocates running workshops and office hours
- Solutions engineers building short POCs with customers

Success metrics (how we judge the codelab):
- Completion rate in self-serve: >= 40% within first session (bench target)
- Time-to-first-successful-response: median <= 15 minutes in workshop runs
- Telemetry visible in Console: token-level and latency traces for every lab run
- Dev feedback NPS >= 4.0 (post-lab quick survey)

High-level structure (manifest):
1) Welcome & intent (5 min)
  - Very short text: what you build, why it matters, what you learn
2) Local quickstart (15 min)
  - Install SDK, set API key, run a single generate call, stream output
  - Repository scaffold created via `rampkit init`
3) Sandbox integration (15 min)
  - Wire a tiny serverless function to the hosted API with env override (SANDBOX_URL)
  - Run smoke tests against a sandbox token limit
4) Observability + Telemetry (10 min)
  - Add the rdesk-telemetry snippet to collect token counts, latency, and model variant
  - Confirm view in Console route dashboard (screenshot step)
5) Failure & fallback lab (10 min)
  - Inject simulated rate limit / model-unavailable response
  - Trigger fallback path to a smaller model and verify functional correctness
6) CI bind & sample PR (10 min)
  - Add minimal CI workflow that runs smoke test and posts basic metrics to a badge endpoint

Module-level details (not exhaustive):
- rampkit init (scaffold):
  - generates simple node/py project with three files: main, tests/smoke, rampkit.yaml (manifest)
  - rampkit.yaml sample keys: name, description, default_model, sandbox_endpoint, telemetry_hooks

- Local quickstart commands (node example):
  - npm i @redwood-inference/sdk
  - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_test_xxx
  - node ./examples/quick-gen.js  # prints streaming tokens
  - Expected output: first streaming token within 3s, final text within 12s (workshop target)

- Observability snippet (py):
  - from redwood import RedwoodClient, TelemetryHook
  - client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  - TelemetryHook.attach(client, project='rampkit-bridge')
  - client.generate(...)
  - Verifier step: Console shows /routes/rampkit-bridge latency and token histogram

Failure & fallback lab specifics:
- How to simulate: set SANDBOX_FAIL_RATE=0.35 in rampkit.env
- Expected behavior: SDK retry once with jitter, then route to fallback model 'redwood-small' per manifest
- Test assertions: smoke test asserts that the final response comes from allowed fallback model and contains fallback footer text

CI integration notes:
- GitHub Actions small workflow: run tests, collect metric JSON, curl POST to internal badge service
- Keep secrets using GitHub Actions OIDC or repo secrets (we show both examples)

Pedagogical design decisions (why this is different):
- Emphasis on observable outcomes instead of just an SDK call. We require a visible Console trace as part of success criteria.
- Short, repeatable checkpoints every ~10 minutes so workshop leaders can triage mid-run.
- Lightweight manifest format that solutions can adapt into customer POCs (rampkit.yaml)

Open questions / decisions to resolve:
- Manifest format: YAML vs JSON? (YAML wins for readability but JSON easier for programmatic edits)
- Should rampkit create a disposable sandbox project in AWS/GCP for workshop runs? Risk: infra overhead vs convenience.
- Telemetry schema: match Console fields (route, model, tokens, latency, customer_id) — need contract with Console team (ticket CONFLUENCE-OBS-678).

Next steps & owner assignments (proposal):
- Draft rampkit CLI prototype (Priya) — 2 sprints (MVP: scaffold + local quickstart)
- Observability contract spec (Liam) — 1 sprint
- Failure injection harness and sample tests (Sofia) — 1 sprint
- Workshop playbook and slide deck (Ethan) — 1 sprint

Notes to self / workshop hints (scratchpad):
- If a participant hits rate limits, show them how to set a `REDWOOD_LOCAL_OVERRIDE` env var to point to a local stub server for debugging
- Keep model outputs deterministic in labs by pinning seed param for generation
- Have a short troubleshooting checklist printed on the workshop handout: API key missing, network proxy, rate limit, wrong region endpoint

Appendix: rampkit.yaml (example manifest snippet)
name: rampkit-bridge-sample
description: Tiny codelab showing SDK to Console path
default_model: redwood-medium
sandbox_endpoint: https://sandbox.redwood-inference.test
telemetry_hooks: [route, tokens, latency, model_variant]
fallbacks:
  - condition: model_unavailable
    target: redwood-small

This doc is intentionally a draft playbook. The aim is to capture the curriculum, the observable success criteria, and the minimal telemetry contract so the Developer Experience and Console teams can iterate quickly.

End of draft.
